key_insight: Rotational equivariance improves learned subgrid-scale closures most when combined with nonlocal receptive fields, yielding better generalization and parameter efficiency for turbulent channel flow.
engineering_relevance: For LES model design, this suggests that physics-aware symmetry constraints can reduce model size and data needs while improving robustness across Reynolds number, anisotropy, and spatial/temporal shifts.
method: Compared data-augmented non-equivariant models against equivariant models
Tested both pointwise and nonlocal architectures at matched parameter counts
Evaluated generalization across spatiotemporal shifts, anisotropy, and Reynolds number
evidence_signal: The equivariant nonlocal model achieved the highest correlation coefficient on every generalization test at roughly half the parameters of its non-equivariant counterpart, and equivariant models were more data-efficient overall.
watch_item: The gains depend on receptive field and dataset characteristics, so pointwise or weakly nonlocal implementations may not outperform simple baselines like Clark in realistic settings.
paper_title: Rotational equivariance and locality in data-driven subgrid-scale closures
